transcript: This beautifully devastating play is as meticulously spun as its main character's everyday existence. Referring to herself in the third person, thegrownwoman (with no spaces) takes us through a consequential day. With various selections of music underscoring her every move, thegrownwoman is a person of routine, discipline, and certainty. Being on her fifth round of IVF treatment, however, is shaking her convictions. While the events of this play are personal and small in scope, they're depicted with the weight of an epic, propped up by an earnest younger version of herself bearing witness, various references to Nigerian culture, and a cathartic final act. Abigail Onwunali's performance is impressively restrained and then impressively open. The way she brings in elements of grief such as denial, bargaining, and reconstruction masterfully illustrate a microcosm of adaptation. The ability to invoke the uncomfortable and sometimes painful experience of adapting to a new reality is what makes the play so effective. If you can get to LCT3 by November 1st, Creation Stories is well worth the trip.
